extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, CRTC officials and staff, regulators, legislators, and other stakeholders in Canadian broadcasting and telecommunications policy
extracted.subtask_description: Recommendations and evaluative criteria for structuring and operating the CRTC (composition of Commissioners, regionalization, procedural rules, public access, resource needs, and decision‑making arrangements) to address changes in broadcasting and telecommunications. Focused on how to design/assess institutional arrangements and procedural practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner time commitment / availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time members have been required to leave other occupations for periods of one or two weeks at a time, brief themselves fully, sit for long hours at public hearings and participate in lengthy business and consultation meetings; the time requirements have excluded from the ranks of potential part-time members persons whose occupation will not allow them to be away frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate suitability of part-time Commissioners by whether their occupations permit frequent absences and long hearings; recognize that heavy time requirements reduce the pool of potential part-time appointees and limit their effective participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of part-time Commissioners in keeping Commission informed of local interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally, part-time Commissioners were to represent the public in various walks of life and to make representations on behalf of local and sectional interests when licensing decisions were under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether alternative mechanisms (public hearings, regional offices, public interest groups) now adequately provide local/sectional input and whether part-time Commissioners remain necessary for that representational purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of part-time Commissioners given complexity/specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: The major issues in broadcasting have grown so complex that they demand a depth of knowledge and expertise that can only be gained by full-time involvement; the position of part-time Commissioners should be phased out as terms expire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider phasing out part-time Commissioners where regulatory issues require sustained specialized expertise; weigh past contributions against current complexity and need for continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting status / fair procedure for Commissioners who sit on hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation in Chapter Four respecting the granting of part-time members a voting status on the applications they hear; scheme attempts to satisfy principles of fair procedure or natural justice given existing situation where part-time Commissioners do sit on public hearings and participate in the decision-making process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Commissioners (full- or part-time) sit on hearings, ensure decision‑making arrangements preserve fairness and natural justice—consider whether those who participate in hearings should have voting rights on the resulting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase number of full-time Commissioners to handle workloads
rubrics_metrics.description: An argument could be made for increasing the number of full-time Commissioners. The current hearing schedule in both sectors leaves Commissioners little time to work on larger policy issues; if the position of part-time Commissioner were phased out, more full-time members would be required to assist in the hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether existing full-time staffing allows Commissioners sufficient time for policy development versus hearing workloads; consider increasing full‑time positions to balance hearings and policy work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralization / regionalization of decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration could be given to the decentralization of the Executive Committee. Complaint that a group of Commissioners all based in Ottawa make decisions affecting what the rest of the country sees; proposal to assign one or more full-time members permanently to each major region with delegated decision-making authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge proposals for decentralization by their ability to put Commissioners in daily touch with licensees and the public, to meet provincial arguments for local jurisdiction, to ease hearing loads, and to improve responsiveness to regional complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Commissioners with delegated authority and regional chairmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional members would be granted decision-making authority and be responsible for hearing and deciding broadcasting applications in their areas; regional offices would operate under a regional chairman who would supervise staff and any Commissioners assigned to his region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating regional posts, ensure clear delegation of authority, appointment of regional chairmen to supervise staff, and mechanisms for coordination with Ottawa to maintain policy uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining uniform policies across regions via regular meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain uniform policies and approaches, it would be necessary for the regional chairmen to meet regularly in Ottawa with the Vice‑Chairman in charge of broadcasting; Ottawa Commissioners could be assigned to sit with regional chairmen on nationally significant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require regular coordination meetings between regional chairmen and Ottawa leadership and reserve mechanisms for Ottawa participation on issues of national significance to preserve policy coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition for major policy and national network licence hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearings involving the development of major policies in broadcasting and licence renewals of the national networks would be conducted by a panel composed of the Chairman, the Vice‑Chairman in charge of broadcasting, and all of the regional chairmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define which matters require expanded panels (major policy or national network renewals) and ensure representation of both Ottawa leadership and regional chairmen in those panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice-Chairmen operational responsibilities split by sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the two Vice‑Chairmen in a new Act would be given operational responsibility for either broadcasting or telecommunications regulation; the Chairman would have over‑all supervision and act as liaison with other government departments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize senior management responsibilities by functional specialization (broadcasting vs telecommunications) while retaining an overall Chair to coordinate policy and external relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of an Ottawa-based review committee with referral powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chairman and two Vice‑Chairmen, situated in Ottawa, could act as a review committee with the power either on its own motion, or of a party to an application, to refer back for re-consideration, to vary or set aside decisions on both telecommunications and broadcasting matters made in any of the regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a central review mechanism to ensure oversight and the ability to correct or revisit regional decisions; include conflict-of-interest safeguards (e.g., substitution if a review committee member sat on the original hearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial/experimental decentralization implementation and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be possible under existing legislation to partially implement decentralization by assigning full-time members to regional offices and appointing standing committees; the regional scheme should be assessed over a period to evaluate effectiveness in processing and deciding applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot regional arrangements before full implementation, set evaluation periods and metrics (processing speed, decision quality, accountability), and be prepared to adjust based on assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sufficiency for regional offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional offices would require sufficient staff and other resources to organize and conduct hearings; procedural innovations that give the public greater access are often costly and under budgetary cutbacks it is difficult to maintain customary practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When expanding regional presence or public access, ensure budgets and personnel are allocated; lack of resources undermines the Commission's ability to maintain public involvement and carry out functions in the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and involvement as a core procedural objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability of the Commission to adequately respond to concerns depends in large part on the degree of access that the public has to the CRTC; a substantial reduction in this access as a result of fiscal restraint would seriously impede the Commission's ability to carry out its functions in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat mechanisms for public involvement (hearings, notices, regional access) as essential elements to preserve; weigh cost savings against the public-interest costs of reduced access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing notice and announcement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requires at least four announcements during a ten day period ending 40 days before the date set for the commencement of the hearing. In the case of AM and FM stations the announcements must be broadcast between 7:00 and 9:00 a.m. or 4:00 and 6:00 p.m. For television stations, the hours are 6:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with detailed public notice schedules for hearings (number, timing, and broadcast windows) to ensure adequate public awareness and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for written replies before oral replies (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission's working paper of July 25, 1978, recommends a change that would require a written reply to interventions before an oral reply would be permitted; other proposals would substantially increase the number of notices of applications required to be broadcast by licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider procedural reforms that front-load written responses to streamline oral hearing time and possibly strengthen the record; evaluate trade-offs in accessibility and administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and prior approval of transactions that 'materially affect' control
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposed that all transactions which 'materially affect' control (defined to mean transactions involving 10% or more of the voting securities) should require prior approval; confirmed in an announcement that such approval would be attached as a condition to licences and renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative thresholds (e.g., 10% of voting securities) as a trigger for prior regulatory approval of share transactions likely to change effective control; apply as licence conditions to preserve supervisory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of ownership and control and rare use of revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission insisted that direct or indirect share transfers that would change effective control must receive prior approval, failing which it would consider revocation proceedings. The Commission has revoked for cause only one licence and failed to renew licences in only three instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain active supervision over ownership/control and reserve revocation or non‑renewal for serious cases; document and justify such exceptional uses of enforcement powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of administrative responsibility by region
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative responsibility for applications is allocated according to the region to which an application pertains; the five regions are British Columbia, the Prairie Provinces, Quebec, Ontario and the Atlantic Provinces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign administrative case responsibility on a regional basis to match local knowledge and logistics; ensure mechanisms for inter-regional coordination where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling flexibility and early tentative dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The flexibility inherent in the CRTC's new method of scheduling and the use of its computer make it possible to assign a tentative hearing date as soon as an application is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt scheduling systems that allow early provisional dates to improve predictability for applicants and stakeholders and to manage hearing calendars efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of applications (appearing vs non-appearing) and staff costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 55% of items were placed on the non-appearing side of the agenda; while this device saves hearing time, staff preparation is the same whether an application is ultimately designated as an appearing or non-appearing item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When categorizing items to reduce hearing time, account for the unchanged staff preparation burden and evaluate net resource impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multi-agency committees of inquiry for coordinated responses
rubrics_metrics.description: For matters calling for a coordinated approach between federal and provincial agencies, the Commission appointed a committee of inquiry consisting of staff members of the CRTC and relevant provincial agencies; the committee submitted a report which was used to call for comments and inform the CRTC decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where issues cross jurisdictions or sectors, form inter-agency inquiry committees, solicit public comments on committee reports, and integrate recommendations into final decisions to ensure coordinated policy outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations governing tariffs: form, content, style and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A document entitled Regulations Respecting The Form And Publication of Tariffs was issued containing details concerning the form, content, style and publication of tariffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize tariff filings by adopting clear regulations on form and publication to ensure transparency, comparability and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to and reliance on statutory policy objectives in Section 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and conditions imposed are designed to further the broadcasting policy enunciated in section 3 (e.g., ownership by Canadians, varied and comprehensive programming, reasonable opportunity for expression of differing views, high standard programming using predominantly Canadian resources); the Commission's role is to decide whether policies and decisions are well calculated to achieve the end sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor regulatory policies and licence conditions to statutory objectives (section 3) and ensure a demonstrable connection between measures and stated policy goals; the Commission has discretion to judge reasonableness of means to achieve statutory ends.
